definitions.explanation: A gender-neutral term for one's husband or wife, often used when speaking about one's own spouse or someone else's.

examples.japanese: {連|つ}れ{合|あ}い⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{旅行|りょこう}→旅行：00748_ryokou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}ってきた→行く：00119_iku⟧。
examples.english: I went on a trip with my spouse.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長年|ながねん}→長年：09684_naganen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{連|つ}れ{合|あ}い⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{亡|な}くした→亡くす：30483_nakusu⟧。
examples.english: They lost their spouse of many years.

examples.japanese: お{連|つ}れ{合|あ}い⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧お⟦{元気|げんき}→元気：00696_genki⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。

notes:
ETYMOLOGY: From ⟦{連|つ}れ{合|あ}う→連れ合う：30484_tsureau⟧ 'to accompany each other.' Literally 'companion.'

REGISTER: Neutral and somewhat old-fashioned — favoured by older speakers about their own spouse. It becomes respectful with the honorific prefix お: お{連|つ}れ{合|あ}い is a polite way to refer to someone else's spouse. For the strictly formal, documentary term, see ⟦{配偶者|はいぐうしゃ}→配偶者：07430_haiguusha⟧.

NUANCE: A warm, traditional term that emphasizes the companionship aspect of marriage. Gender-neutral, making it useful when the speaker doesn't want to specify husband or wife.

CONTRAST WITH OTHER TERMS:
・⟦{夫|おっと}→夫：00982_otto⟧ / ⟦{妻|つま}→妻：01005_tsuma⟧ — formal for own spouse (documents, etc.)
・⟦{旦那|だんな}→旦那：12330_danna⟧ / ⟦{奥|おく}さん→奥さん：02853_okusan⟧ — common colloquial terms
・⟦{主人|しゅじん}→主人：00987_shujin⟧ / ⟦{家内|かない}→家内：00958_kanai⟧ — traditional, becoming less common
・⟦パートナー→パートナー：11287_paatonaa⟧ — modern, gender-neutral loanword
